Results.ReviewText:
I purchased my Spirit II back in April to compliment my 22" Kettle. Some nights when I get home Late I just cant wait to heat up the charcoal to make dinner. That being said, this is my 3rd propane grill, and 1st from the Weber collection.

The Good: The cast iron grill is amazing! I really did my home work before purchasing this grill and some peopler were complaining about food sticking. I think one of two things was happening, not properly pre heating the grill, and not using Weber's no stick cooking spray. I get perfect sears on all my steaks with this grill. The heat displacement is amazing! It feels even across the surface and I don't feel like there are any hot/cool spots; just an even temp displacement. I kissed flare ups goodbye with this grill. The heat shields work perfectly and I get an amazing sear. 

The Bad: I wanted to give this grill 5 stars; it's originally what I was going to rate it. I have a short list of areas for improvement. One, the stainless steel table tops are pretty easy to scratch up just from placing some cooking tools on the table. So, I tend to lay a wood cutting board on the table top to help prevent that. I'm also not a fan of the table folding in on the left hand side. It can make it a bit of a pain when moving it around, I understand it's for storage purpose but I have considered replacing the bolts for the table with screws that would hold it in place permanently. I've seen some people scratch up some of the interior while removing the warming rack too. It took me a second to Last jab at the grill is I purchased this item in red. There are some areas on the lid that have some flaws or almost look like some black specks where I suppose it wasn't painted quite right, nothing worth complaining about but I am writing a review so I thought I'd mention it. 

All in all this is an amazing grill. The price and the few flaws I had mentioned are the only reason I didn't give it a 5 star. I'll probably end up replacing the tables years down the road. The grill is easy to clean, cooks like a dream, is easy enough to move around with the large wheels. It's a top notch product and I doubt I'll ever buy anything other than a Weber again

Results.ReviewText: I purchased this grill upon retiring my 19 year old weber.  The old frame finally had rusted.  19 years later I purchased my new grill for less than the one I did 19 years ago.  At first I thought it alarming that they had to have really cut corners.  Nope.  I think the new grill is better engineered and the manufacturing tolerances are tighter than ever.  The attention to detail from the welded nuts already in place, to the plastic washers that won't scratched the parts so they don't rust is awesome.  Everything was in the box, no missing pieces and although it took me several hours I feel really good about the quality of things.  What also struck me was putting on the grill cover.  I though it would be difficult but it slid right down.  There are no sharp edges, no 90 degree corners for the cover to get hung up on.  Great Job Weber!  I suspect I will get another 19 years from this one.  I not sure there will be a next one.  I may be too old to grill any longer at that point.

Results.ReviewText: This is my second Spirit grill; the first was a Spirit two burner. It cooks as good as ever, and I really like the new propane tank holder design. The frame engineering leaves much to be desired, and after following the assembly instructions to a T, I have run into multiple issues that are minor but nonetheless annoying. First, the two little plastic feet that are supposed to be hammered on with a rubber mallet would not stay attached after the grill was assembled. Then, one of the wheels fell off while carrying it up a few deck stairs. The space-saving fold down shelf (still an awesome feature, and one of the main reasons we bought our original Spirit grill!) is supposed to be used to move the grill, but it never feels secure, and has even slipped out in transit. I like the big wheels for moving the grill in grass, but the whole design of using the foldable shelf as a handle just feels half-baked. In all, I’m happy with the grill, especially if I don’t have to move it, but these minor issues just seem like something that should have been taken care of in the R and D phase.
Results.Title: Quality cooking, questionable construction

Results.ReviewText: The last gas grill I had used lava rock. It ruined a LOT of meat. I swore I would never have another gas grill. But, that was many years ago and since then many of the flare up issues have been fixed. Yesterday was the first test of my new Weber Gas Grill. We were going to have some beautiful Porterhouse Steaks for dinner but I wanted to test this grill out and season it with cheaper meats first. I cooked a grill full of burgers first, with no problems and then some fatty brats. I stayed right there and watched. It did flare up a little but stayed manageable. They turned out great. Finally the steaks. I got nice grill marks and the flavor was great. So far, I am happy with the grill. It heats up fast and has plenty of heat. I have always been a fan of charcoal grills because I like good smoky flavor. You get good smoky flavor with this grill, it's just not hickory or oak. I think I will order a smoke tube and experiment with that. I like the convenience of a gas grill. Turn on the gas, fire it up, this grill heats up fast, cook it up and your done. If you use charcoal, do you have charcoal on hand? Lighter fluid? Are you just wanting to cook some hot dogs? A few burgers? A Steak or two? It can be a waste of charcoal pretty easily. This grill produces good results faster and easier. I'm impressed so far!
Results.Title: Happy So Far

Results.ReviewText:
Purchased a Weber Spirit 2 burner grill 25 years ago and it still works like new today (one set of new burners, one set of SSteel grills/flavorizer bars, a few igniters over the years). Needed a larger 3 burner grill for entertaining, so bought this new 3 burner version.  

The E-310 is improved in nearly every way. Taller lid so that I can cook vertical "beer can chickens,"  greatly improved grease collection system, 3 powerful burners, two usable side tables, the temperature gauge is finally in the right place (the middle of the lid instead of on the side), much better igniter system, much smoother burner controls that can make finer adjustments, no more rubber end plugs on the chassis (which used to fall out after a few years), much improved gas gauge, and I prefer the "open cart" design of the area under the grill vs. the enclosed pedestal with doors found on some Weber models (hard to keep clean of bugs, etc.).  

IMO, the very best feature of this Weber is that it has a much larger area for indirect heat cooking (roasts, ribs, ham, fish).  Very useful!

Reliability: I expect this one to last as long as my previous Spirit, which is still happily grilling for my son's family!

Cons?  Just one that prevents me from giving a 5 star rating;  the left side table folds down and is supposed to be used as when moving the grill (one hand on either side and lift to put the grill on its wheels to move like a cart).  This mechanism needs serious redesign, the table will pop out of its upper locking lugs no matter how carefully this is done.  Moving the grill using this side table will eventually damage the table so that it will not lock.  And I need to move our grill each time that it is used.  [One more Con that is not really about the grill, Weber's grill cleaning sprays and non-stick cooking sprays don't work very well.]
Results.Title: My 2nd Weber Spirit in 25 Years!
